html:
A kingdom of the Dagomba people in northern Ghana, founded about the 15th century by horsemen whose tradition names Naa Gbewaa as ancestor, with its later capital at Yendi.

It is related to the Mamprusi and to the Mossi kingdoms to the north. Muslim traders and clerics settled at its court, and Islam spread among its rulers from the 17th and 18th centuries. Dagbon paid tribute to Asante from the 1740s. Its king, the Ya Na, still reigns; the killing of the Ya Na in 2002 led to years of conflict between two royal houses, settled only in 2019. See also Salaga.
sum: A kingdom of the Dagomba people in northern Ghana, founded about the 15th century by horsemen whose tradition names Naa Gbewaa as ancestor, with its later capital at Yendi.
